html:
The Inga dams are two hydroelectric dams at the Inga Falls on the lower Congo river, about 225 km southwest of Kinshasa. Inga I opened in 1972 and Inga II in 1982.

At Inga the Congo, the river with the second largest flow in the world, drops about 100 metres through a series of rapids. Engineers have long seen it as the greatest hydropower site on earth. A full "Grand Inga" scheme could, on paper, produce more than twice as much power as China's Three Gorges Dam.

The first two dams were prestige projects of Mobutu. A very long power line was built to carry their electricity to the copper mines of Katanga, partly to keep that rebellious province dependent on the capital. Debt, poor upkeep and war left the dams running far below capacity for years, while most Congolese still have no electricity.

Plans for a third dam, Inga III, have been announced many times with foreign partners, but have not been built, as costs, politics and the needs of local people have stood in the way.
sum: The Inga dams are two hydroelectric dams at the Inga Falls on the lower Congo river, about 225 km southwest of Kinshasa. Inga I opened in 1972 and Inga II in 1982.
